source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Christian Religious Education, Grade 5
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). First published 2017, Revised 2024. 5 strands: 1.0 Creation, 2.0 The Bible, 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, 4.0 The Church, 5.0 Christian Living (30 sub-strands total). Note: sub-strand 2.7 is titled 'God's Protection' in the front-matter Summary of Strands and Sub Strands table and in the strand-body running header row, but the actual body text (outcomes/experiences/KIQ) for that slot is titled '2.7 The Birth of Moses' and covers Exodus 2:1-10 (Moses hidden in the Nile, found by Pharaoh's daughter) — not the Mount Carmel/Daniel-style protection narratives covered elsewhere in the Bible strand. Body text is treated as authoritative here (per the same precedent used for the Grade 6 CRE 3.4 discrepancy); 'God's Protection' is retained parenthetically as the table's thematic label since the story's KIQ ('How was Moses protected by God?') is itself framed around protection. Appendix 1's Suggested Assessment Methods table lists this same slot as '2.7 God's protection' with a 3-lesson allocation matching the body header. Sub-strand 3.9 'A Friend at Midnight' is allocated 5 lessons (vs 3 for every other Bible/Life-of-Jesus sub-strand) consistently across all three locations in the source (summary table, body header, Appendix 1) — not a discrepancy, an intentional extended allocation.

subStrands.name: 1.1 My Purpose (Talents and Abilities)

apply lessons learnt from the parable in their day-to-day life

How do you nurture your talents, gifts and abilities?

write on flash cards activities they like doing at home, school and in church
in groups, discuss how the activities they have listed aid in nurturing their talents, gifts and abilities

in pairs, list what they want to become in future
discuss why it is important to live a purposeful life
in turns, read Matthew 25:14-30 on the parable of the talents and narrate how different talents were used

read James 1:17A and say what they have learnt

English: reading skills are applied as they read Bible texts.
Creative Arts: the skill of performing is enhanced as they compose and sing songs.

scopeNotes: The nine gifts of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:1-11) are: word of wisdom, word of knowledge, faith, gifts of healing, working of miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, speaking in different kinds of tongues, interpretation of tongues.

The fruit of the Holy Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23) is: love, joy, peace, patience (longsuffering), kindness, goodness, faithfulness, humility (gentleness/meekness), self-control — nine qualities, explicitly named in the source's Pertinent and Contemporary Issues note for this sub-strand.
